note: Threat-evidence backfill: real conformance test at crates/chio-conformance/tests/threats/capability_token_theft.rs imports chio_kernel_core::capability_verify::verify_capability_with_floor and exercises the production single-entry verifier (Lane B1). Three deny-asserting arms cover the canonical stolen-token sub-vectors: (1) ScopeSuperset attack class -- a signed token whose scope is widened post-mint fails the canonical-JSON signature check with CapabilityError::InvalidSignature; (2) PartialSignature attack class -- a signed token whose issuer is re-targeted to an attacker key fails the issuer-trust check with CapabilityError::UntrustedIssuer; (3) post-expiry replay fails with CapabilityError::Expired. A round-trip sanity arm pins that legitimate tokens still verify, blocking over-rejection from silently making the row green. The test header documents the revert-to-prove-it-fails recipe (delete the trusted_issuers guard or the canonical-JSON signature check in verify_capability_with_floor).
